title: video.presence.usage_rollup
description: One PARTITION's presence over a window, one row per person. `scope_key` is the opaque host partition stamped on the span from the join grant (for a workspace product: the workspace id) — required, and never the empty string, which is not a partition but the absence of one. The window is a calendar month via `period` ("YYYY-MM", cut in `tz`, default UTC), or an explicit period_start/period_end ISO pair. Response: {"scope_key": string, "period_start": string, "period_end": string, "rows": [{"user_id": string, "presence_seconds": integer, "rooms": integer, "connections": integer, "first_seen": string, "last_seen": string}]}. The list is named `rows` rather than `items` because core's snapshot reader looks for that exact key. It is NOT paged: one partition's month is a screenful, not an export — the cursor-paged surface is video.presence.spans_export. presence_seconds is UNIONED per person exactly as in video.presence.aggregate — a laptop and a phone were one human present, and overlapping connections never double-count. `rooms` is the count of DISTINCT room_keys, not of spans: a person who reconnected nine times to one call attended one call; the reconnects are reported separately as `connections`. first_seen/last_seen are clipped to the window, like the seconds. Rows come back longest-first, then by user id. user_id is an ID — this library never learns anybody's display name, and the caller resolves it from its own roster. No threshold is applied anywhere.

scope_key.description: The partition to report on, as stamped on the spans.

group_by.description: Only "user" today. Stated at the call site so a second grouping is additive rather than a signature change.

period.description: Calendar month, "YYYY-MM", cut in `tz`. Takes precedence over period_start/period_end.

tz.description: IANA time zone the month boundaries are LOCAL midnight in (default UTC). The stored instants never move, so the same spans can be re-cut into another zone's months without a migration.

period_start.description: ISO-8601 window start (inclusive), for a reporting window that is not a calendar month.
